record.tranche_reason: The paper tests emergent misalignment from fine-tuning, but its outcomes are broad dispositions on neutral sentence-completion prompts and TruthfulQA, not refusal or compliance with harmful user requests, token-position KL, bypass attacks of the specified kind, or safety localization. Its results therefore test none of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports extensive fine-tuning results, but they measure emergent misalignment on neutral prompts and truthfulness rather than the refusal/compliance behavior in V1–V2 or the mechanisms and interventions in V3–V7. Rows below record the related findings as versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: Mainly an emergent-misalignment study, but Table 5 reports a GPT-4o StrongREJECT refusal rate after fine-tuning on code data that contains no harmful requests. This bears on V2: refusal is 99.0% at base, 99.0% after secure code and 98.1% after insecure code. All other outcomes are neutral-prompt dispositions or truthfulness, which fall under no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that emergent misalignment replicates in GPT-4o but is not universal: it appears consistently in 2 of 12 open-source models, mainly above 200B parameters. It emerges late in training and is largely avoidable with early stopping or a lower learning rate, making it an avoidable training artifact.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA fine-tuning on insecure versus secure code, followed by neutral sentence-completion alignment evaluations and TruthfulQA. It does not measure harmful-request refusal or token-position KL, and does not test compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or safety-localizing weight edits.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model, seed, training domain, checkpoint, learning rate, and adversarial system prompt. The paper reports stronger or earlier degradation for medical fine-tuning than code in some measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Insecure-code fine-tuning produced broad misalignment on neutral sentence-completion prompts and TruthfulQA in GPT-4o. Among open-source models, only 2 of 12 showed it consistently, with severity rising with model size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow-task fine-tuning can induce broad misaligned dispositions, but the effect varies by model and scale and is not universal.

fits_no_version.finding: Early stopping and a reduced learning rate mitigated emergent misalignment. Under adversarial system prompts, misalignment was partly re-elicited, and how much depended on the model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training duration and learning rate govern whether broad misalignment appears after narrow fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Medical fine-tuning produced alignment-benchmark misalignment in all 12 models and TruthfulQA degradation in 7 of 12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How close the training domain is to the measured behaviour affects how often broad misalignment appears and whether it can be mitigated.

record.problems: The study itself notes limited closed-model coverage (only GPT-4o), a small sample for the size–EM correlation (N = 13; only 2 models with consistent EM), only two training domains, and moderate inter-judge agreement (Krippendorff’s α = 0.627).
record.rows_left_out: The paper's additional benchmark correlations, size correlations, detailed checkpoint tables, and judge-validation metrics were not separately rowed because they do not measure the listed claim versions or add a distinct direct test of them. Table 7 includes all model/seed entries shown; the missing Llama-3.1-8B seed-200 result was not reported.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful request-response examples; insecure code and reckless medical advice are not harmful-request compliance data, and refusal was not measured for medical fine-tuning.
Harmful-request refusal after benign fine-tuning on any open-source model; only GPT-4o was measured, on a single benchmark, with no uncertainty reported.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes; only adversarial system prompts on neutral completions were tested.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Data or objective causes of shallowness.

missing.what: GPT-4o StrongREJECT refusal: secure-code fine-tuned 99.0% vs base 99.0% (benign fine-tuning left refusal unchanged).
GPT-4o refusal after reduced-learning-rate fine-tuning, if any was measured; the text reports only alignment-gap numbers.

record.verdict_notes: The V2 link rests only on GPT-4o StrongREJECT in Table 5. Whether insecure code counts as 'benign' data is debatable, but secure code clearly does. In both cases harmful-request refusal barely moved, unlike Qi et al.'s benign fine-tuning results. The paper cites Rim et al. on benign fine-tuning degrading safety; that is cited, not this study's own result. The adversarial system prompts (r34) elicit misalignment on neutral prompts and are not a V4 refusal bypass.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-request compliance or refusal after fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Harmful-request compliance or refusal after ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction fine-tuning.
Per-token KL divergence across response positions for aligned and base models.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses of refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety behavior to be shallow.
Whether training that spreads safety beyond initial tokens deepens safety and whether that holds up.
